# Complete customer review and analyst receiving

Use Node 24 or later for the analyst application. The customer HTML uses an
ordinary current browser with JavaScript, Web Crypto and IndexedDB. Its report,
original files, review model and editor are all embedded; it needs no server,
installation, API credential or network connection.

## Prepare the original briefing

Open the existing analyst project using Applications → Economic client briefing
and customer review, or:

```sh
starforge economic-client serve --project /private/original-economic-project
```

Use Sources and Client briefing to retain the actual selected data and save a
complete report edition. The existing OECD companion operation remains available.
A source-only OECD briefing can be reviewed without an EconData credential. A
selected EconData acquisition uses the existing named credential and provider
terms. Read the complete source terms and attribution before delivering data.

The Customer reviews view requires a saved briefing, intended reviewer and label.
Create the package once, then download review.html and its complete review.json.
Keep the operation ID after an interrupted creation; the same input returns the
same package. A new requested package is a new original operation.

Every package includes the complete original report JSON, HTML, observation CSV
and SOURCE_RIGHTS.json. It also includes all original selected companion files,
including its source rows, rights and saved project archive, plus each selected
native EconData decoded response, numeric lexemes, wrapper type tags and original
wire body. Source periods, historical duplicates and exact values are unchanged.
The package ID binds the entire content; the complete files are verified before
an editor or receiving workspace accepts them.

The operational bound is 512 MiB for the complete JSON input and aggregate
decoded review files/source bodies. Base64 and JSON increase document size.
A full project also has its existing 512 MiB uncompressed packet bound. The
application reports an over-limit result and retains the original source project;
it never substitutes a truncated report.

## Customer's offline operation

Open the exact downloaded review.html. First inspect the original full report
and source/companion downloads. The editor offers the report, its original
series, individual original observations and companion editions as review targets.
Search and paging change only the visible target list; all original data remains
inside the same document.

For a selected target, record Approved, Question or Change requested and comments.
The report summary/editorial notes and a series's title, interpretation or
methodology accept an explicit proposed text. Observation values, units, source
classification, periods and original captures are read-only. A question about
them remains bound to the original observation, including its absolute native
position, so repeated historical periods are not confused.

The browser retains the working draft by package and review identity. Save
revision adds a content-bound edition containing all current decisions and notes.
Repeated saving without a semantic change returns the same edition. The document
retains the full parent-linked edition chain, up to 1,000 saved editions, and an
unfinished draft. Download Working HTML before moving to another browser or
machine; IndexedDB by itself is local browser state.

Return JSON saves the complete current revision before exporting. Send that
original file back through the agreed customer channel. It contains every
original package member and the complete review history, not a list of comments
separated from their source. The intended-reviewer label describes the operation;
it is not a digital signature or proof of a person's identity.

## Analyst's returned-file operation

Select the complete Return JSON in Customer reviews. Its original bytes and
receiving operation are retained locally before upload. Continue original return
receiving after an interrupted transport; the same file and operation reopen the
same saved return. A rejected selection remains retained; select the corrected file with a new receiving attempt. Different branches or later review editions receive distinct
return identities. Nothing replaces an earlier return.

Save any open editorial draft before comparing the return. The comparison shows
the original editorial text, current draft text, customer proposal and complete
original target/source binding. Choose explicit dispositions:

- Acknowledge records that the analyst read the decision.
- Use proposal applies the selected editorial text to the current draft.
- Defer records a remaining decision.
- Reject records the analyst's disposition and notes.

A changed current value is displayed as a conflict. Applying a proposal over it
requires its explicit checkbox as well as the retained current-value hash. A
proposal for an original series no longer present in the draft cannot be applied
to another capture automatically. Refresh and compare again after another draft
save; an old project revision or comparison digest is rejected.

Only selected decisions on the visible page are submitted. Save those dispositions
before changing pages. The complete received review remains available and every
disposition operation records the original return, comparison, current values,
proposal, reason, and before/after draft. The application does not send mail,
publish a briefing, change source observations or infer acceptance from a comment.

Save the resulting draft as a new complete report edition. The former editions,
return bytes, working package and disposition history remain available in the
same project. Export complete project carries every corresponding object and the
original EconData and OECD source histories. A fresh receiving workspace verifies
them all before adoption; repeating its identical received packet returns the
current project without discarding later edits.

## CLI and installed client

All normal action inputs are JSON files; retain the original operation ID and
exact input after a lost response.

```sh
starforge economic-client review-create --project /private/project --operation client-review-01 --input /private/review-create.json --output /private/package-receipt.json
starforge economic-client review-download --project /private/project --id ORIGINAL_PACKAGE_ID --name review.html --output /private/review.html
starforge economic-client review-receive --project /private/project --operation client-return-01 --input /private/customer-return.json --output /private/return-receipt.json
starforge economic-client review-preview --project /private/project --input /private/selected-return.json --output /private/comparison.json
starforge economic-client review-resolve --project /private/project --operation client-disposition-01 --input /private/dispositions.json --output /private/disposition-receipt.json
```

Create input is {briefing_id, recipient, label}; selected-return is {return_id}.
Disposition input contains return_id, expected_revision, comparison_sha256 and
decisions[]. Each selected decision supplies target_id, current_sha256, action,
reason and optional confirm_conflict:true. Use the actual values returned by
review-preview. Do not invent a current hash or reuse a different return.

For an active operator, use its existing private connection:

```js
import {readConnection,createClient} from "./client.mjs";
const connection=await readConnection("/private/project/connection.json");
const client=createClient({baseUrl:connection.base_url,token:connection.token});
const packageReceipt=await client.action("review-create",selection,originalOperation);
const html=await client.reviewFile(packageReceipt.id,"review.html");
const accepted=await client.receiveReview(originalReturnBytes,originalReceivingOperation);
const comparison=await client.action("review-preview",{return_id:accepted.id});
```

Do not open a second file owner while the browser owns the project. The server
serializes its original actions, raw returned-file receiving and full exports.

## Complete actual receiving course

Use receive-review.mjs with examples/review-receiving.json adapted to the actual
existing project and saved briefing. Every named directory and input is private.
Set return_file and resolution_file to the real files the customer and analyst
will produce; they may not exist on the first invocation.

```sh
node products/economic-client/application/receive-review.mjs --input /private/original-review-course.json
```

The first run creates and downloads the complete offline review and returns
WAITING_CUSTOMER_REVIEW. Open and use it. Save actual review choices, close/reopen
the working HTML, inspect the retained decisions and export the Return JSON to
the selected path. Repeat the same command.

The course receives that complete original return, confirms same-operation replay
and retains each immutable comparison plus current-comparison.json, then returns WAITING_ANALYST_DISPOSITION if the
actual dispositions are not present. Read the current original comparison and
save its explicit selected choices to resolution_file. Repeat the same command.

It applies those choices, saves a following report, retains every report file,
exports the whole reviewed project, receives it into the configured separate
customer directory twice using the same packet, closes it and independently
reopens the original return, dispositions and report bytes. Source acquisition
and buyer operations are not replayed by this course.

The result RECEIVED_AWAITING_RENDERED_INSPECTION describes the remaining real
work. Open the exact received project and review files, inspect all applicable
attachments and exercise them as described below. It is not a source-only READY
label. The course journals each completed native result; after process loss keep
its original input, working directory and output archive.


## Rendered product inspection — owner instruction, 2026-10-13

This applies to every current, future, resumed and delegated worker, across providers and local or cloud runtimes. The required inspection standard is: “that includes all attachments and this does not become review theatre or test theatre you need to literally observe the actual thing the way a user would see and use it”.

Before presenting a client/prospect-facing application, website, dashboard, demo, report, presentation, export or any attachment, the producing peer must open/run/render the exact outgoing version, LOOK at it and normally use it as the recipient would. View the actual screenshots you capture. Inspect the actual presentation/screenshare width and relevant narrow/mobile width, important user controls, populated/empty/loading/error states, downloads and reopened exports. Open the usable contents of ZIPs/projects and every applicable report/PDF page. Source review, schemas, HTTP 200, DOM counts, tests, checklists and another worker's approval cannot substitute for observing and using the actual product.

Fix broken, unstyled, cramped, clipped, overflowing or unreadable output within the authorized work before presenting it. Use plain industrial software design: readable tables, clear hierarchy, consistent typography and spacing, restrained controls, useful labels and responsive layouts. Preserve real workflows, source data and computations. Inspection must lead directly to repairs and continued delivery; it must not replace implementation/integration or become repeated checking. Keep validation focused on the actual remaining risk. Do not run broad test sweeps, repeat accepted checks, build a verification product or create review bureaucracy or an approval queue.

For video and audio: “also add that if u make a video use voice gen tts not robot voices, use generative stuff we have models, use them”. Use available high-quality generative voice/TTS and useful generative media, with natural professional delivery. Actually watch/listen to the final outgoing export, including pacing, pronunciation, timing and audio alignment. Preserve existing spending, voice and attribution controls.

Include this complete instruction in delegated assignments and the active owner-controlled provider/project/cloud policy, boot, build and receiving guidance those workers actually read. Reuse already updated copies and return exact updated paths/version in the original policy thread with the next substantive result. Delivery of source does not establish that every runtime loaded it. Preserve all other owner controls and original operation identities; leave historical records and third-party/vendor policies intact. This instruction creates no restarts, watchers, credential gate or new release permission and does not revive owner-stopped work. When a runtime is unavailable, join the existing equipped receiver with the complete exact version and opening steps, review its actual rendered result, and continue independent implementation while it runs.

# EconData original source acquisition

This client is the source-acquisition component of the saved economic client briefing workspace. It reads the existing EconData API, retains complete original responses, joins native metadata, and transports the same source journal to a receiving customer workspace.

## Original authority and dependencies

The complete primary contracts are included under the product's `upstream/` directory:

- Codera's original Swagger 2 document at <https://www.econdata.co.za/sdmx-codera/swagger.json>, 95,052 bytes, SHA-256 `40c9a7c4671b948586bd31ebdd32a38e68c2de8c5701f5af610ec37465a3d0b9`.
- The released MIT-licensed `coderaanalytics/econdatar` 4.0.4 source, commit `9a2f5ed2130122c461c05f3b880c5c4f3ed8f911`, annotated tag object `16d23978f43c3352d19e20c14e3ca94297501c47`. The complete selected R functions cover authentication, registry/data reading, pagination, release conversion and metadata. Their original file identities are in `upstream/ECONDATA_SOURCES.json`.
- Maintained MIT-licensed `lossless-json` 4.3.1, original published UMD distribution, 9,626 bytes, SHA-256 `3eebf0821060a4d9910c55e6c50f11961062cc20944ee745007ea19e3cdec885`. The unchanged distribution, license and original npm release metadata are under `application/vendor/`.

Swagger documents request paths and query types but does not define the response schemas. The released R consumer supplies the native typed-message, dataset, release, metadata-reference and pagination contracts. The client keeps those original response bytes and exposes an untagged lossless projection.

Use Node.js 20 or later. Node builtins supply filesystem durability, HTTPS, SHA-256 and response decompression. The included original lossless parser is the sole runtime dependency; there is no package installation step.

## Application API

```js
import { createEconDataClient } from './econdata-client.mjs';

const client = createEconDataClient({
  directory: '/private/client-workspace/econdata',
  credentialEnv: 'ECONDATA_CREDENTIALS',
  baseUrl: 'https://www.econdata.co.za/sdmx-codera/v1',
  timeoutMs: 120000,
  maxResponseBytes: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
});
```

Configuration contains environment variable names. An existing `client_id;client_secret` value follows the released R client's Cognito client-credentials exchange. An existing API JWT value is used as the original bearer token. An optional `credentialsEnv` selects a service-credential-only variable instead of `credentialEnv`. The default token endpoint is `https://codera-econdata.auth.af-south-1.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/token`; an explicit authorized deployment can supply `authUrl`.

Construction and source inspection, export, and import do not inspect credential values or make HTTP calls. A workspace containing only its original OECD companion can use the same customer handover. Credential values and OAuth response bodies remain process memory and are excluded from source journals and exports.

Each acquisition method uses a caller-supplied operation ID. Reusing that ID with the same exact selection continues its original sources and frozen release. Reusing it with different input is rejected. A new requested edition gets a new operation ID.

### Registry

```js
await client.registry(operationId, {
  kind: 'datasets', // datasets | dataflows | datastructures | codelists
  agencyids: ['ECONDATA'],
  ids: selectedIds,
  versions: ['latest'],
  detail: 'full',
  relations: 'references',
});
```

The three plural filters accept native comma strings or explicit arrays of strings. The result has `schema`, `state`, `operation_id`, `selection`, `records`, `structures`, `sources`, `acquired_at`, and `number_encoding`.

The dataset catalogue does not document a `detail` query. The original selection retains it while the actual catalogue request omits it. Dataflow, DSD and codelist requests use the documented parameter. Every returned next link is consumed.

### Capture

```js
await client.capture(operationId, {
  dataset: { agencyid: originalAgency, id: originalId, version: originalVersion },
  release: { kind: 'latest' },
  // Or {kind:'description', value: originalDescription},
  // {kind:'timestamp', value: originalTimestamp}, or {kind:'unreleased'}.
  series_keys: selectedNativeQueryStrings,
  start: originalStart,
  end: originalEnd,
  hist_obs: true,
});
```

Omit optional keys instead of passing undefined or null. Omitting `series_keys`, or passing an empty array, requests the selected dataset. A nonempty list contains unique native query strings. The original returned `series-key` value remains its actual scalar, object or array type.

The catalogue resolves the selected agency, ID and version to one original dataset before capture. A native reference is formed from its full returned triplet; it is never reverse-split on hyphens. A `latest` or description release is resolved once from the native release list and retained before dataset requests. A missing description needs a corrected new selection. It never silently chooses another release.

The released R reader treats timestamps returned by the release catalogue as UTC, then formats the request in Africa/Johannesburg. This client preserves the complete original release row and the separate exact query string. An explicit offset-bearing timestamp is converted to the same provider timezone. An explicit timestamp without an offset is already the provider's local query wall time. `unreleased` omits the release query and is marked mutable. `hist_obs` remains independent of release selection.

The complete result is:

```text
schema: tjl.econdata.capture.v1
state: COMPLETE
operation_id, selection, dataset_ref, release
datasets: complete native dataset objects with merged series[].obs[]
structures: complete returned registry collections
structure_sources: original source ID and projection pointer for each structure
metadata_joins: dataset → provision agreement → dataflow → DSD → concepts/codelists
series_sources: each source/page/filter/series observation range
sources: complete original GET response identities
acquired_at
number_encoding: json-number-lexeme-string
```

The client joins the dataset's original provision agreement, its dataflow, the dataflow's DSD, all component concept schemes, and every referenced codelist. This includes codelists used by attributes. Missing complete referenced schemes or lists are fetched through their documented native GET. Every original structure field is retained. The join records the native component, its actual original `native_type`, source ID and projection pointer, selected concept, scheme reference and optional codelist reference. A native component without a type wrapper has `native_type: null`; no Dimension/Attribute/TimeDimension/PrimaryMeasure type is inferred.

Every actual `Link: …; rel=next` is followed through the complete chain. Next pages must retain the original API authority, endpoint and frozen selectors. Offset and limit can advance. Each selected series filter has its own chain.

Datasets merge by the full native agency/ID/version. Series merge by the canonical value of their original `series-key`, preserving scalar, object or array types. Observations concatenate in received page order. Historical repeated periods and overlapping-filter memberships remain in the result, with `series_sources` identifying their complete source, selector, page, native series index, observation offset and count. Conflicting non-observation metadata raises a retained attention outcome.

### Explicit documented reads

```js
await client.read(operationId, {
  resource: 'datasets',
  ref: nativeDatasetReference,
  section: 'release',
  query: { latest: true },
});
```

Supported resources are datasets, dataflows, datastructures, codelists, conceptschemes and provisionagreements. Dataset sections are release, schema and series; the series section optionally takes `series_ref`. Only each endpoint's documented query names and native types are admitted. This method returns complete `responses[]` with their source IDs, projected data and numeric-token maps, plus full `sources[]`.

## Exact numeric and native source values

`parseEconDataJSON(rawText)` uses the unchanged lossless parser. Every JSON numeric token becomes its exact lexical string, including integer digits beyond JavaScript precision, trailing decimal zeros, exponent notation and tiny values. Native JSON strings remain strings. The accompanying `number_lexemes` maps original JSON pointers to numeric tokens, so a reader can distinguish native strings from projected numbers.

Only native two-element wrappers whose first value begins `#sdmx.`, `#sdmx:` or `#sdmx/` are unwrapped. Ordinary arrays and localized `["en", "label"]` values remain arrays. Complete raw responses preserve all original wrapper types. `type_tags` maps untagged projection JSON pointers to their original wrapper tags, independently of the raw numeric-token pointers. Nested wrappers at one pointer retain their ordered original tags.

```js
const received = client.readSource(sourceId);
// {source, raw_text, data, number_lexemes, type_tags}
const status = client.inspect(operationId);
// Complete result, or exact saved attention/progress/frozen selection.
```

Every body is read from its retained relative path and checked against its original SHA-256 and byte length. Original wire bytes and decoded JSON bytes both survive content encoding. Ordinary acquisition requests ask for identity encoding; gzip, deflate and Brotli are decoded only after their complete original wire body is retained. Duplicate object keys are rejected by the maintained parser.

## Native acquisition and continuation

The client journals the operation and request before the actual GET. Each attempt retains its complete headers, status, HTTP version, wire body and terminal result. A process interrupted after writing a complete HTTP envelope can reuse that envelope. A short body, incomplete framing, unsupported encoding or invalid JSON remains retained for diagnosis and a later explicit continuation.

Requests use one configured HTTPS authority and original bearer session. The source directory freezes its authority once any source operation exists. An empty source directory created for an OECD-only export may still select its first actual EconData authority. Redirects are recorded individually and must remain within that API authority and path. There is no automatic request retry or alternate identity. A returned 401 clears only the in-memory service token; a later explicit continuation can obtain the current token. Provider Retry-After deadlines are retained and enforced across subsequent operations.

The response byte limit and deadline are explicit controls. Exceeding them produces an attention outcome with the original saved selection and response prefix. It does not mark a partial page as complete. A caller can increase its local configured resource bound and continue the same operation.

Sensitive response header fields such as Set-Cookie and authentication-info are omitted with their names recorded. Authorization request values and token response bodies never enter source packets.

A process-owned native directory lock serializes source mutation. Linux uses the original PID, boot and process-start identity. Other Node hosts conservatively retain a live PID binding. Stale owner recovery preserves the previous lock record. Customer transfer omits machine locks and imports into the receiver's own directory.

## Full source export and independent reopening

```js
const packet = await client.exportState();
const receiver = createEconDataClient({
  directory: '/private/received-customer/econdata',
  credentialEnv: 'CUSTOMER_ECONDATA_CREDENTIALS',
});
await receiver.importState(packet);
const capture = receiver.inspect(originalOperationId);
```

The source-state packet contains the complete original operation and GET journals, all complete body objects, attempt response records and retained prefixes, the original API authority, and the provider delay record. Every member has a safe relative path, exact base64 content, byte count and SHA-256. A manifest binds the ordered member identities.

Import validates the complete packet before writes, rejects links and conflicting existing members, and preserves original IDs and journal bytes. An interrupted receive can repeat the same packet into the same receiving directory. Completed captures reopen without network or credential values. Pending operations retain their frozen native version/release and original source requests, while the receiving customer chooses its environment variable name.

The surrounding client-briefing project retains this complete packet with its editable source selection, report objects and untouched original OECD project archive. Source account access and source distribution rights remain attached to the actual provider and selected data; an API capture does not create new data rights.

# Complete native receiving course

The included receive-native.mjs runs the actual installed original OECD engine, the economic client application and a fresh receiving workspace. It accepts one original input and writes a durable stage journal. Repeat the same command/input after interruption.

## Native prerequisites

- Node 24 or later and the complete application source including its native source client and vendored parser.
- The existing complete installed OECD source graph and its actual Python executable. The selected original client module must have access to its maintained source/parser dependencies.
- Separate private directories for the receiving journal, source client project, customer client project, original OECD project and receiving OECD project.
- For optional EconData acquisition, actual authorized source credentials in the selected environment variable, exact dataset/release/series selection, and the complete reviewed source-use terms.

The public-source course needs the original official OECD source already included in that installed project. It does not contact a subscriber source when no EconData selection is supplied.

## Run the complete course

Copy examples/receiving.json to the operator's private directory and replace every absolute path with the actual selected host path. Keep operation_id stable.

    node /absolute/application/receive-native.mjs \
      --input /private/original-economic-client-receiving.json

The same native command continues its original journal and project. Each source or save action retains the original immutable operation/input. A completed step's exact returned result is adopted on continuation.

The course performs these connected product actions:

1. Open the original client project and seed its installed OECD source.
2. Save the original native OECD briefing and a notes revision in the same source project.
3. Attach the complete revised native report, rows, dataset descriptor and project ZIP.
4. When configured, acquire the selected original EconData source and its complete metadata/history.
5. Save a complete client report edition and an editorial revision.
6. Compare the original native observation groups and retain the comparison JSON.
7. Download every report file from both editions, preserving its full original hash/size.
8. Export the complete client project, close it, and receive that archive into the separate named customer workspace.
9. Download both customer report editions and compare their complete original bytes.
10. Import the same original OECD ZIP into the fresh native customer project; compare every original report file and original rows/snapshot.
11. Close and reopen the customer application, then read all saved report files again.

Its final JSON identifies the complete archive, both original OECD briefings, both client editions, project directories, receiving journal and actual browser launch command. receiving.json retains the full native stage results, errors and exact operation binding.

## Actual rendered-product delivery

**Applies to every current and future peer, provider, local session and cloud worker.** Before calling a client/prospect-facing app, website, dashboard, demo, report, presentation or export ready, the producing peer must open, run or render the exact outgoing version, look at its actual rendered screen or real screenshots, and operate its important user controls. Capturing screenshots without viewing them is insufficient. Inspect the actual screenshare width and narrow/mobile width where relevant; inspect populated, empty, loading and error states, downloads, exports and reopening.

econdata_credentials <- function() {
  if (!requireNamespace("tcltk", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package \"tcltk\" needed for this function to work.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  tkn <- NULL # Need to add global bindings for variables
  token   <- tcltk::tclVar("")

  tt <- tcltk::tktoplevel()
  tcltk::tkwm.title(tt, "econdata.co.za credentials")
  tkn.entry <- tcltk::tkentry(tt, textvariable = token)

  reset <- function() tcltk::tclvalue(token) <- ""
  reset.but <- tcltk::tkbutton(tt, text = "Reset", command = reset)

  submit <- function() {
    tkn <- tcltk::tclvalue(token)
    e <- parent.env(environment())
    e$tkn <- tkn
    tcltk::tkdestroy(tt)
  }
  submit.but <- tcltk::tkbutton(tt, text = "Submit", command = submit)

  tcltk::tkgrid(tcltk::tklabel(tt, text = "Enter Token Details"),
                columnspan = 2)
  tcltk::tkgrid(tcltk::tklabel(tt, text = "API Token"),
                tkn.entry, pady = 10, padx = 10)
  tcltk::tkgrid(submit.but, reset.but, pady = 10, padx = 50)

  tcltk::tkwait.window(tt)
  return(tkn)
}

get_metadata <- function(x) {
  env <- fromJSON(system.file("settings.json", package = "econdatar"))
  if (nchar(Sys.getenv("ECONDATA_URL")) != 0) {
    env$repository$url <- Sys.getenv("ECONDATA_URL")
    env$registry$url <- Sys.getenv("ECONDATA_URL")
  }
  if (nchar(Sys.getenv("ECONDATA_AUTH_URL")) != 0) {
    env$auth$url <- Sys.getenv("ECONDATA_AUTH_URL")
  }


  # Fetch data structure definition (metadata) ----

  # Provision agreement
  attrs <- attr(x, "metadata")
  provision_agreement_ref <- paste(attrs[["provision-agreement"]][[2]]$agencyid,
                                   attrs[["provision-agreement"]][[2]]$id,
                                   attrs[["provision-agreement"]][[2]]$version,
                                   sep = "-")
  response <- GET(env$registry$url,
                  path = paste(c(env$registry$path,
                                 "provisionagreements",
                                 provision_agreement_ref), collapse = "/"),
                  add_headers(authorization = get("econdata_token",
                                                  envir = .pkgenv)),
                  accept("application/vnd.sdmx-codera.data+json"))
  if (response$status_code != 200) {
    stop(content(response, type = "application/json", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  }
  data_message <- content(response,
                          type = "application/json",
                          encoding = "UTF-8")
  provision_agreement <- data_message[[2]]$structures[["provision-agreements"]][[1]]
  # Dataflow
  dataflow_ref <- paste(provision_agreement[[2]][["dataflow"]][[2]]$agencyid,
                        provision_agreement[[2]][["dataflow"]][[2]]$id,
                        provision_agreement[[2]][["dataflow"]][[2]]$version,
                        sep = "-")
  response <- GET(env$registry$url,
                  path = paste(c(env$registry$path,
                                 "dataflows",
                                 dataflow_ref), collapse = "/"),
                  add_headers(authorization = get("econdata_token",
                                                  envir = .pkgenv)),
                  accept("application/vnd.sdmx-codera.data+json"))
  if (response$status_code != 200) {
    stop(content(response, type = "application/json", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  }
  data_message <- content(response,
                          type = "application/json",
                          encoding = "UTF-8")
  dataflow <- data_message[[2]]$structures[["dataflows"]][[1]]
  # Data structure definition
  data_structure_ref <- paste(dataflow[[2]][["data-structure"]][[2]]$agencyid,
                              dataflow[[2]][["data-structure"]][[2]]$id,
                              dataflow[[2]][["data-structure"]][[2]]$version,
                              sep = "-")
  response <- GET(env$registry$url,
                  path = paste(c(env$registry$path,
                                 "datastructures",
                                 data_structure_ref), collapse = "/"),
                  query = list(relations = "references"),
                  add_headers(authorization = get("econdata_token",
                                                  envir = .pkgenv)),
                  accept("application/vnd.sdmx-codera.data+json"))
  if (response$status_code != 200) {
    stop(content(response, type = "application/json", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  }
  data_message <- content(response,
                          type = "application/json",
                          encoding = "UTF-8")
  data_structure <- data_message[[2]]$structures[["data-structures"]][[1]][[2]]
  concept_schemes <- data_message[[2]]$structures[["concept-schemes"]]
  codelists <- data_message[[2]]$structures[["codelists"]]


  # Compile metadata ----

  concepts <- list()
  for (component in data_structure$components) {
    id <- component[[2]][["concept-identity"]][[2]]
    repr <- component[[2]][["local-representation"]]
    concepts[[id$id]] <- list(type = component[[1]],
                              concept = NULL,
                              codelist = NULL)
    for (concept_scheme in concept_schemes) {
      if (id$agencyid == concept_scheme[[2]]$agencyid &&
            id$parentid == concept_scheme[[2]]$id &&
            id$parentversion == concept_scheme[[2]]$version) {
        for (concept in concept_scheme[[2]]$concepts) {
          if (id$id == concept[[2]]$id) {
            concepts[[id$id]]$concept <- concept[[2]]
          }
        }
      }
    }
    if (is.list(repr)) {
      for (codelist in codelists) {
        if (repr[[2]]$agencyid == codelist[[2]]$agencyid &&
              repr[[2]]$id == codelist[[2]]$id &&
              repr[[2]]$version == codelist[[2]]$version) {
          concepts[[id$id]]$codelist <- codelist[[2]]
        }
      }
    }
  }
  data_provider_ref <- provision_agreement[[2]][["data-provider"]][[2]] |>
    (function(x) do.call(sprintf, c("%s:%s(%s):%s", x)))(x = _)
  dataflow_ref <- provision_agreement[[2]][["dataflow"]][[2]] |>
    (function(x) do.call(sprintf, c("%s:%s(%s)", x)))(x = _)
  data_structure_ref <- dataflow[[2]][["data-structure"]][[2]] |>
    (function(x) do.call(sprintf, c("%s:%s(%s)", x)))(x = _)
  metadata <- list(data_provider_ref = data_provider_ref,
                   dataflow_ref = dataflow_ref,
                   data_structure_ref = data_structure_ref,
                   concepts = concepts)
  return(metadata)
}

## Connecting to econdata.co.za

In most cases reading and writing data from econdata.co.za requires you to authenticate yourself. This usually requires you to enter an API token which you can get from the web application. Log in to the web application and go to the *Account* page, click on *Show key* and copy the API token by clicking anywhere on the token itself. Paste this token into the dialogue box that appears when running `read_dataset` for example and click *Submit*.

If you are using a service account you can set the `ECONDATA_CREDENTIALS` env variable with the format `client_id;client_secret` in order to automate the above process.

If you are connecting to econdata.co.za through a portal other that the main site (someportal.econdata.co.za rather than www.econdata.co.za) you will need to set the `ECONDATA_URL` and `ECONDATA_AUTH_URL` env variables, please contact econdata@codera.co.za for further details.

Please see the [EconData blog](https://econdata.co.za) for in depth tutorials
